findings.reason: by the plan's own standard the roadmap widening must be the measured, intended change the ledger and evidence wideners are, so §16 should record the binder's base/head output for every plan beside those pins rather than leaving it unaccounted.
findings.text: §16 requires the six section-spelling expressions be composed from the one shared number core `\d+(?:[.-]\d+)*`, but `_SECTION_WORD_RE` binds a comma/and-separated list of *bare* numbers `\d+`, so threading the core in widens it to accept a dotted or hyphenated number (`section 5.1` would newly bind where today the match ends at `section 5`); §16 explicitly pins the same broadening for `ledger.normalize_section` and `evidence._section_key` with a base/head test and records "no stored value moves", yet says nothing about roadmap's binder, whose output feeds relationship wiring and could shift on the two plans that carry dotted section ids

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 hides raw-text boundary location, section identity, card recognition and heading level behind the one private span parser, exposed as two small public projections (`plan_headings` and the kept `structured_section_spans`), so callers bind to named records rather than re-walking the document.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 mandates that every reported section-spelling expression be recomposed from the one exported number core, which includes roadmap's own `_SECTION_WORD_RE` at reckon/roadmap.py:170, whose per-number token is today a bare `\d+`; the plan pins the identical widening for the ledger and evidence grammars but records nothing for roadmap's.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16/§17/§18 add four public definitions in total (one `strip_tags`, two in `_plan_html.py`, one classification predicate), each section states why no public name can be retired (the readers keep callers), and §16 states no refusal family is added, so no section adds to cli_options, mcp_views or refusal_families without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — searched reckon/ and confirmed every mechanism the implementable sections cite exists at the named file, including `_TAG_RE` and `count_open_decisions` (reckon/_plan_html.py:1506,1514), `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94), `section_record_id`/`_SECTION_IDENTITY` (reckon/crew/routing.py:219,224), the store helpers `_H2_OPEN_RE`…`landed_section_ids` (reckon/_store.py:848–1093), and the schema declaration readers; the plan extends these rather than adding a parallel subsystem.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two public functions §16/§17 add (`strip_tags` over the existing `_TAG_RE`, and the machinery-element predicate) each add behaviour over an existing private expression and are public only because their consumers cross the package boundary, which each section states.
